extracted.intended_audience: Congress, the Secretary of the Interior, Indian Bureau officials, land officers, and policymakers overseeing federal Indian affairs
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, policy objectives, and statutory requirements enacted by Congress and explained by the Secretary of the Interior governing Indian protection, settlement, appropriation of funds, procurement, land disposals, and trust-fund management in the late 19th century.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy goal — employ Indians as agriculturists or herders
rubrics_metrics.description: "To set the Indians to work as agriculturists or herders, thus to break up their habits of savage life, and to make them self-supporting."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Secretary of the Interior's stated policy objectives; presented as a programmatic aim to raise Indians to self-support by fostering agricultural/herding habits rather than immediate forced change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy goal — educate Indian youth of both sexes
rubrics_metrics.description: "To educate their youth of both sexes, so as to introduce to the growing generation civilized ideas, wants, and aspirations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education is an explicit policy instrument for introducing 'civilized' ideas and promoting long-term assimilation/advancement; supports industrial and practical training as later provisions indicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy goal — allot parcels in severalty and grant individual title
rubrics_metrics.description: "To allot parcels of lands to Indians in severalty, and to give them individual title to their farms in fee, inalienable for a certain period, thus to foster the pride of individual ownership of property."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement in severalty and conferring of individual title are central to policy; intended to individualize Indians and replace communal tribal landholding gradually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy goal — dispose of unoccupied reservation lands with tribal consent to form funds
rubrics_metrics.description: "When settlement in severalty with individual title is accomplished, to dispose, with their consent, of those lands on their reservations which are not settled and used by them, the proceeds to form a fund for their benefit."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disposal of surplus reservation lands is conditioned on tribal consent; proceeds are to create funds to reduce federal appropriations; intended as a step in transition to ordinary citizenship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy goal — ultimately treat Indians like other inhabitants under U.S. law
rubrics_metrics.description: "When this is accomplished, to treat the Indians like other inhabitants of the United States under the laws of the land."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final aim of the policy chain; Secretary emphasizes gradualism and use of tribal authority as a vehicle rather than immediate forcible abolition of tribal relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory equal civil rights (1870 statute)
rubrics_metrics.description: "All persons within the jurisdiction of the United States shall have the same right in every State and Territory to make and enforce contracts, to sue, be parties, give evidence, and to the full and equal benefit of all laws and proceedings for the security of persons and property as is enjoyed by white citizens."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee interprets the statute as securing to Indians ample and valuable rights; acknowledges potential contrary interpretations but urges broad construction to include Indians; enforcement, however, may be difficult in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: End of treaty recognition (1871 act)
rubrics_metrics.description: "...in future no Indian nation or tribe within the territory of the United States shall be acknowledged or recognized as an independent nation, tribe or power, with whom the United States may contract by treaty."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks a major change in federal policy: pre-existing treaties remain valid but future treaty-making with tribes is prohibited by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of federal criminal laws to Indian country and statutory crime provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal statutes provide penalties for encroachment on Indian lands, theft or injury to Indian property, and specified crimes against persons and property within Indian country; and general laws of the United States extend to Indian country for crimes committed within exclusive jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A body of penal statutes exists to protect Indians and Indian property; effective protection depends on enforcement and local judicial capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for enforcement and supportive public opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Although statutes exist to protect Indian rights, enforcement is hindered by Indian ignorance of legal remedies, remoteness and lack of courts, hostile local white populations, and the Indians' readiness to resort to violence; public opinion and Christian citizens must be enlightened to secure effective protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislation alone insufficient; successful enforcement requires educating Indians, establishing accessible legal mechanisms, and shaping public sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: President-authorized police regulations bill (proposed 1879)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed bill empowering the President to establish police regulations for Indian reservations, punish crimes on reservations and in Indian Territory, and confer jurisdiction upon State and Territorial courts and U.S. district courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported favorably but not enacted at the time of the report; identified as desirable additional legislation to improve protection of Indians' personal and property rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation purposes must be specified: subsistence, civilization, education, employee pay, incidental expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriations are made for specific purposes: care and support, subsistence and civilization, support/education/industrial schools, pay of employees, incidental expenses of Indian service, telegraphing and contract expenses, and specific payments to named persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriations in statute specify intended uses (with itemized sums for tribes/agencies) and include provisos and reporting requirements on how funds are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement/public notice rule for purchases over $500
rubrics_metrics.description: No purchase of supplies for which appropriations are made exceeding in the aggregate five hundred dollars in value at any one time shall be made without first giving at least three weeks' public notice by advertisement, except in cases of exigency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In exigency the Secretary may direct open-market purchases up to $3,000, provided an official record of the facts constituting the contingency is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing restriction on distribution of goods and authority to reallocate surplus funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Goods and supplies purchased for the fiscal year shall be immediately available for purchase, but no goods or supplies shall be distributed or delivered to Indians prior to July 1, 1880; Secretary, under the President, may use any surplus in appropriations to purchase subsistence to supply deficiencies up to $50,000 in the aggregate, but funds appropriated to fulfill treaty obligations shall not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any diversions under this authority must be reported in detail to Congress at its next session with reasons for diversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against permitting Indians to enter Texas
rubrics_metrics.description: All officers and agents of the Army and Indian Bureaus are prohibited, except by special direction of the President, from granting permission in writing or otherwise to any Indian or Indians on any reservation to go into the State of Texas under any pretext whatever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any officer or agent violating this provision shall be dismissed from the public service. The Secretary of the Interior is directed to take reasonable measures to prevent such entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in use of employee appropriations with safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: When not required for the purpose for which appropriated, funds provided for the pay of specified employees at any agency may be used by the Secretary for the pay of employees at such agency, but no deficiency shall thereby be created; specified employees may be detailed for other service when not required for their original duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriations for millers, blacksmiths, engineers, carpenters, physicians, and treaty-provided articles may be diverted to other uses for the benefit of the tribes within the President's discretion and with the consent of the tribe; the President must report actions under this provision to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchase preference and reporting for Indian manual and training schools
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Interior is authorized whenever advantageous to purchase for use in the Indian service from Indian manual and training schools articles manufactured at such schools in the manner customary among individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts of such transactions shall be kept in the Indian Bureau and in the training schools, and reports thereof made from time to time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/exclusion for agency employee counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers and Indians employed at agencies in any capacity shall not be construed as part of agency employees named in the specified section of the appropriations act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to clarify who counts toward statutory employee limitations and payroll provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding and pay rates for Indian police
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriation for services of not exceeding 800 privates at $5 per month each, and not exceeding 100 officers at $8 per month each, of Indian police, and for equipments and rations, to be employed in maintaining order and prohibiting illegal traffic in liquor at the several Indian reservations, seventy thousand dollars (statutory example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutorily-prescribed ceilings on numbers and pay rates are used to fund reservation police forces; related provisos about employee counting apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust-fund management — deposit in U.S. Treasury in lieu of investment and interest payments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Interior may deposit sums held as trustee for various Indian tribes in the U.S. Treasury in lieu of investment when he believes the best interests of the Indians will be promoted; the United States shall pay interest semi-annually from date of deposit at treaty-stipulated or law-prescribed rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows converting trust investments into Treasury deposits with semi-annual interest paid in the usual manner without further appropriation; also authorizes semi-annual crediting of certain accounts (e.g., L'Anse and Vieux de Sert bands) under prior acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment and reappropriation of small trust proceeds and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific small proceeds (e.g., sale of sheep and wool) may be reappropriated to other tribal uses (example: refund to Sioux funds reappropriated for Yankton Sioux); Secretary must report actions under provisos to Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute demonstrates that proceeds may be reallocated for tribal benefit but calls for congressional accounting and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement cap and exigency record requirement (alternative phrasing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in exigency (officially recorded by Secretary), purchases normally require three weeks' advertisement for amounts over $500; in exigency Secretary may authorize purchases up to $3,000 in open market with official record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiteration of procurement safeguards: public notice and recordkeeping for exceptions to ensure accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms for completing payment for Kansas trust and diminished-reserve lands
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons included under prior acts may complete payment for lands at newly appraised value with credit for sums already paid; the balance shall be paid in three equal installments, first due Jan 1, 1881, remaining annually; installments draw interest at 6% per annum from date of last payment received; those in possession who failed prior payments must make entry and pay in three installments; bond required for timbered lands to prevent waste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute prescribes how existing claimants and entrants may complete purchases: appraisal, credits, installment schedule, interest rate, bonds for timbered lands, and consequences for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of actual settlement sufficient for Kansas lands
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual settlement shall be regarded as sufficient where claimant actually resides on contiguous land to which he holds legal title and has heretofore cultivated and made valuable improvements on his adjoining claim in good faith for the purpose of a home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides evidentiary standard for who qualifies as an 'actual settler' for entry and payment privileges under the act, subject to compliance with law and General Land Office regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default/forfeiture and resale procedures for trust/diminished-reserve lands
rubrics_metrics.description: If a settler defaults on payment, his claim and money paid shall be forfeited and the land offered for sale after notice; unsold lands may be disposed to actual settlers only; upon nonpayment of installments lands with default for 90 days are listed and proclaimed for sale; sold once per year; unsold lands may be offered for private entry in quarter-section tracts; tax sales do not defeat U.S. purchase-price rights but tax purchaser may redeem by paying unpaid purchase price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute establishes procedural steps for handling defaults, public offerings, minimum prices, annual offerings, private entry options, taxation effects, and redemption rights to protect federal financial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees, proceeds, and administrative rulemaking for disposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Register and receiver receive same fees and commissions as for public land disposal; net proceeds after expenses are deposited to the credit of the proper Indian fund; Secretary of the Interior shall make all rules and regulations necessary to carry the act into effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative mechanics for sale, accounting, and delegation of rulemaking authority to implement statutory disposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest rate for installments (Osage/related acts)
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases arising under the act, interest at the rate of five percent per annum shall be computed and paid upon all that part of the purchase money in respect to which time is given for the payment of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the statutory interest rate for installment purchases in certain acts (example provided in CHAP.107 Sec.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification of Ute agreement with conditional amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance and ratification of agreement submitted by Ute chiefs is conditioned by amendment: withhold payments to White River Utes ('the proportion of the money... coming to White River Utes, except for removal and settlement') until surrender or apprehension of guilty parties or President's satisfaction they are not living or have fled beyond U.S. limits; also add presidential discretion to appropriate up to $10,000 for education in schools within/beyond selected lands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congress ratifies the agreement but inserts conditions to withhold funds pending satisfaction of criminal-surrender conditions and authorizes executive discretion for limited educational appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term annuities to named individuals (Ute settlement)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the portion of moneys coming to the White River Utes, the United States shall pay annually to specified named persons certain sums respectively during twenty years, if they live so long (lists of named individuals and amounts included).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute creates individualized annuity obligations tied to ratified tribal agreements; demonstrates Congress can earmark portions of settlement funds for named beneficiaries with temporal limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory reporting and accounting oversight requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Various provisos require the Secretary to report to Congress at its next session concerning actions taken under diversion authorities, purchase-from-school transactions, and other discretionary uses of appropriations; specified reappropriations are directed to be charged to trust funds and accounted for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes congressional oversight: discretionary diversions and special purchases must be documented and reported to preserve transparency and trust accounting.
